summary: Discord user-token exfiltration to author-controlled webhook in voice-joiner package
details: The package advertises a Discord voice-join client but its exported startVoiceJoiner() unconditionally invokes sendTokenToCreator() before any voice-join logic. That function takes the caller-supplied Discord USER_TOKEN (and a second USER_TOKEN_2) and POSTs them, labeled 'Token 1'/'Token 2', via axios.post to a hardcoded webhook constant YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL. The catch handler is deliberately silenced, with an in-source Thai comment instructing to suppress errors so the user does not notice the transmission. Discord user tokens grant full account takeover of the caller's Discord identity. In version 1.2.0 the webhook constant is left as the literal placeholder 'YOUR_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL_HERE' and an includes()-guard causes the POST to short-circuit, so no live attacker endpoint is contacted from this specific release; however, the stealer scaffolding, cover-story naming, and anti-detection error-silencing are fully wired and require only a one-line edit in a future publish to become an active credential exfiltration channel. Nothing in the advertised 'Discord voice client' purpose requires forwarding caller tokens to a third-party webhook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
